notes: An image fixture: the resume arrives as a PNG, so every value depends on OCR quality and there is no native text to fall back on.

Synthetic, and drawn rather than photographed: a single-column ATS-friendly layout rendered at 150 dpi in greyscale, with no resolution metadata, which is what a screenshot or a phone photo also carries.
Deliberately plain: one column, no tables, no graphics, standard section headings, and metadata lines separated by pipes. It is the shape a resume is in when it is trying to be read by a machine.
The header tagline reads 'Registered Nurse | Medical-Surgical & Post-Operative Care'. Only the first half is a job title; the second names a specialization, as in fixtures 1, 2 and 6.

The employers are hospitals rather than 'Co., Ltd.' companies, which is new to this corpus: NER reads 'Riverside General Hospital' as a location, not an organization, and returns 'St. Bernadette Medical Center' as four spans, two of them starting mid-word.
